chapter: Fish fries, passing the hat and district living
title: Dawson on drinking, Jim Robinson and his father
summary: Dawson says he still drinks, that a musician who can't drink is dead, and mentions his father drinking into his nineties.

story.theme_name: Drink, drugs and the bandstand's casualties
story.community_name: Drugs and drink on the bandstand and the road

blocks.x: Do I drink? Any more? Any more? I drink what I can get. Do I drink? Yes, I did. I drink liquor. Any more. That hell of a day's all do I drink. It's cheap. Day and time I go down to the bootleg down to preservation. I don't go across the street and get me a hardball.
Could you drink with Buddy Petit?

Take Jim Crow to tell you, kid, I drink. Jim Crow used to knock out some robber. That's a fellow can drink, though. Jim Robinson. I say, oh. You ain't got nothing? No. I said, shut up. You know, that gives you a good spirit, you see. A fellow's dead, if you can't drink nothing, if you ain't. You just as dead as you can be. I don't care how good you can play. can play. You just can't. You make a lot better when you get a little couple of drinkers. I know how. I've been drinking ever since I've been doing myself. Ever since I was old enough to get out. And I lived to be this age, you know, and it wasn't hurting me. My daddy drank lick up until he died. He was about ninety-some-odd years old when he died.
